_note: Hand-corrected against grith v0.3.1 (binary reports 18 active filters). The upstream generator reads crates/grith-docgen/data/filters.toml, which still carries pre-0.3.1 score ranges, stale summaries and two unregistered modules (semantic, outbound_binaries). Re-running `npm run gen:references` will revert this file until that TOML is fixed in the grith repo.

filters.name: Operation risk scoring
filters.summary: The baseline every call starts from, priced by operation class: routine spawn 0.5, non-routine spawn 1.0, HTTP 0.5 without a body and 1.0 with one, category-2 syscalls and namespace primitives 5.0.

filters.name: Static path matching
filters.summary: Fifteen anchored path rules from paths.toml, scoring 3.0, 4.0 or 5.0. SSH private keys are the 5.0 case; ~/.aws and ~/.gnupg are 4.0.

filters.name: Sensitive path heuristic
filters.summary: Prices credential-shaped paths that no static rule names, in bands of 0.5, 1.5, 3.0, 4.0 and 4.5. A system config read is the 0.5 case.

filters.name: Allowlist / denylist
filters.summary: Operator allow and deny rules, plus approvals persisted from digest review. A denylist hit adds 3.0; an allowlist hit subtracts 1.0 - one of only two filters that can lower the composite.

filters.name: Argument length & structure
filters.summary: Flags argument shapes rather than content: oversized strings, encoded payloads and shell metacharacters in unexpected positions.

filters.name: Capability enforcement
filters.summary: Scores 10.0 on all three of its paths, well past the 8.0 deny line. Ships with an empty grants file, so it runs permissive until an operator writes one; an unreadable capabilities.toml stops the daemon starting.

filters.name: Secret / credential scanning
filters.summary: 1618 patterns for provider keys, tokens and private-key material, scoring 3.0 to 5.0. A low-signal generic match scores 1.0. The single largest cost in registry startup.

filters.name: Command structure analysis
filters.summary: Twelve rules from commands.toml scoring 2.0 to 4.0: piped curl-to-shell, sudo running arbitrary scripts, base64 payloads in subshells, fork bombs.

filters.name: Destructive action
filters.summary: Hard-denies irreversible host or storage destruction at 9.0 - filesystem format, raw block-device overwrite, recursive delete of a system root or a database data directory. Backups and data mounts land in the 3.5 to 5.0 queue band instead.

filters.name: Egress policy
filters.summary: Destination policy, banded by mode. The shipped mode is review, so a deny-band destination scores 6.5 and a review-band one 3.5. An unknown DNS name is a soft 0.5; a data-bearing DNS qtype adds 2.0.

filters.name: DLP gate
filters.summary: Scores secrets found in outbound arguments, banded by policy: redact-and-allow 1.0, queue-for-review 5.0, deny 9.0. The shipped policy is queue-for-review.

filters.name: Canary detection
filters.summary: Scores 9.5, deliberately above the deny line, when a registered canary token reaches an outbound sink. Checks HttpRequest, NetConnect, ShellExec, ProcessSpawn and FileWrite/FileAppend paths - reading a canary file is not a detection.

filters.name: Destination reputation
filters.summary: Static domain lists only, not the learned trust table: known-malicious 4.0, raw IP 3.0, suspicious TLD 2.0, known-safe -1.0, anything unknown 0.0.

filters.name: Behavioural anomaly
filters.summary: Compares the call against the session baseline once 200 calls exist. A mild deviation scores 1.0 and a significant one 3.0; all three numbers are operator-tunable.

filters.name: Taint tracking
filters.summary: Scores an operation that follows a read of tainted data at 3.0, 4.0 or 5.0 by taint level. Spawn data-flow variants score 1.5. The registry entry expires after an hour.

filters.name: Session containment
filters.summary: The 600-second scoring window opened by a containment signal: network 4.5, process spawn 4.0, shell 3.5, reduced to 2.0 for control-class unix sockets. The sticky session-lifetime lock is a separate mechanism.

filters.name: Rate limiting
filters.summary: Per-operation-type volume caps scoring 1.0, 2.0 or 3.0. Burst penalties are risk-gated by default, so routine high-volume work does not accumulate score on its own.

filters.name: Egress rate
filters.summary: Per-destination outbound rate and burst detection, 1.5 to 5.0 - the beaconing and fan-out shapes a single call cannot show. Gated by proxy.filters.egress.enabled, not by an egress_rate key.
